clinician.trajectory_summary: An 89-year-old female with a 40-year history of stable CLL presented with worsening dyspnea and dry cough. Initial labs on admission (Day 1) showed leukocytosis (WBC 67x10^3/uL) and thrombocytopenia (platelets 72x10^3/uL), with otherwise normal electrolytes and renal function, but respiratory acidosis. On Day 2, the patient developed oliguric acute renal failure (creatinine 1.63 mg/dL, BUN 55 mg/dL), significant hyperuricemia (20.4 mg/dL), hyperphosphatemia (Pi 7.8 mg/dL), mild hypocalcemia (8.3 mg/dL), and elevated LDH (966 U/L), leading to a differential diagnosis of Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS). Conservative treatment with IV fluids, bicarbonate, febuxostat, and sevelamer was initiated. On Day 3, the patient became anuric with further deterioration of blood tests, including severe hyperphosphatemia (Pi 26 mg/dL), severe hyperuricemia (42 mg/dL), severe hypocalcemia (7.2 mg/dL), severe hyperkalemia (6.94 mmol/L), worsening azotemia (BUN 107 mg/dL, creatinine 2.2 mg/dL), and metabolic acidosis. At this point, a diagnosis of TLS was confirmed, and urgent long hemodialysis was initiated.
